title: Finite Bessel's Inequality: Projection Identity Gives Nonneg Remainder
content: bessel_finite proves ∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² for any finite orthonormal set s directly from Mathlib's Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le. The mathematical content: the orthogonal projection projₛ x = ∑ᵢ∈s ⟨vᵢ,x⟩·vᵢ satisfies ‖x - projₛ x‖² = ‖x‖² - ∑ᵢ |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² (projection identity, a consequence of orthonormality + Pythagoras). Since ‖x - projₛ x‖² ≥ 0, the inequality follows. bessel_monotone and bessel_insert are corollaries: adding vectors to an orthonormal set can only increase the Bessel sum (monotonicity under set inclusion).
mathContext:
\text{orthonormal} \{v_i\}_{i \in s} \Rightarrow \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x \rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2\\
\text{Proof: } \left\|x - \sum_{i \in s} \langle v_i, x\rangle v_i\right\|^2 = \|x\|^2 - \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \geq 0\\
s \subseteq t \Rightarrow \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \sum_{i \in t} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2

title: Infinite Bessel's Inequality: Bounded Partial Sums Converge
content: bessel_inequality proves the infinite case ∑' i, |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² for any orthonormal family indexed by an arbitrary type ι, via Orthonormal.tsum_inner_products_le. The key step: the partial sums ∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² are bounded above by ‖x‖² for all finite s (finite Bessel), so by monotone convergence the tsum is bounded. bessel_summable (line 114) is the summability companion: the family i ↦ |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² is square-summable (belongs to ℓ¹), a fact that also follows from the bounded partial sums argument. This is the first appearance of Fourier coefficient decay: ⟨vᵢ,x⟩ → 0 as i → ∞ in a suitable sense.

title: Parseval's Identity: HilbertBasis Isometry to ℓ²
content: parseval_identity proves ∑' i, |⟨bᵢ,x⟩|² = ‖x‖² for a Hilbert basis b of an inner product space E. This is the equality case of Bessel's inequality — holding when the orthonormal system is complete (a Hilbert basis). The proof chain: HilbertBasis.repr is a linear isometry b.repr : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] ℓ²(ι,𝕜), so ‖b.repr x‖ = ‖x‖. Then lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum converts ‖b.repr x‖² (the ℓ² norm squared) to ∑' i, ‖(b.repr x)(i)‖² = ∑' i, ‖⟪bᵢ,x⟫‖². parseval_norm_sq (line 147) gives the equivalent ‖x‖² = ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖² form useful for norm computations.
mathContext:
b \text{ Hilbert basis of } E \Rightarrow \sum_i |\langle b_i, x\rangle|^2 = \|x\|^2\\
\text{Via: } b.\text{repr} : E \xrightarrow{\sim_{\ell^2}} \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{k})\\
\|b.\text{repr}\, x\|^2 = \sum_i \|b.\text{repr}\, x(i)\|^2 = \|x\|^2

title: Bessel Recovers Cauchy-Schwarz: Singleton Orthonormal Set
content: bessel_extends_cauchy_schwarz proves that applying Bessel's inequality to a singleton orthonormal set {i} recovers |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² via simpa with Finset.sum_singleton. This is the bridge connecting the two inequalities: Bessel's inequality is the multi-vector generalization of Cauchy-Schwarz for unit vectors. inner_le_norm (line 167) takes one more step: from the squared inequality |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖², nlinarith derives |⟨vᵢ,x⟩| ≤ ‖x‖ — the pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz bound for unit vectors. Together these show that Bessel strictly subsumes Cauchy-Schwarz for the case of unit vectors.
mathContext:
s = \{i\},\; \|v_i\| = 1 \Rightarrow |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2 \quad (\text{Cauchy-Schwarz})\\
\text{Bessel: } \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2 \xrightarrow{|s|=1} |\langle v, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2\\
|\langle v, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2 \Rightarrow |\langle v, x\rangle| \leq \|x\| \quad (\text{nlinarith})

title: Bessel Summary: Unified Statement Answering OQ-04
content: bessel_summary collects the three main results into a single conjunction: (1) finite case ∑ᵢ∈s |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖², (2) infinite case ∑' i, |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖², (3) summability of the coefficient sequence. The proof is a triple anonymous constructor ⟨fun s => ..., ..., ...⟩ — each component is a single Mathlib lemma. This consolidated theorem directly answers OQ-04: YES, Bessel's inequality for orthonormal systems can be formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib's Orthonormal API, itself a consequence of the iterated Cauchy-Schwarz and Pythagoras theorem in inner product spaces.
mathContext:
\text{bessel\_summary}:\\
(1)\; \sum_{i \in s} |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2 \quad (\text{finite})\\
(2)\; \sum_i |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2 \quad (\text{infinite})\\
(3)\; i \mapsto |\langle v_i, x\rangle|^2 \in \ell^1 \quad (\text{summable})

title: ℓ² Norm Formula: Connecting HilbertBasis.repr to Concrete Inner Products
content: parseval_norm_sq expresses ‖x‖² = ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖² — the norm of x in terms of the ℓ² norm of its HilbertBasis coefficients. A key technical step is lp.norm_rpow_eq_tsum, which for p=2 gives ‖f‖² = ∑' i, ‖f i‖² for f in ℓ². Combined with HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply (b.repr x i = ⟪bᵢ, x⟫_𝕜) and the isometry ‖b.repr x‖ = ‖x‖, this three-step chain makes the abstract isometry concrete: the abstract norm is the familiar sum-of-squares of Fourier coefficients.
